method: Researched and written with web-search verification, revised in a second pass with current vendor documentation; then fact-checked independently by a second agent, which read every string in ch1.json and every <text> label in ch1-fig-1..4.svg, fetched the live Anthropic pages on October 12, 2026 (Prompting best practices, Best practices for Claude Code, Define success criteria and build evaluations, Structured outputs) and compared each quotation word for word, confirmed the OpenAI GPT-5.5 guide wording, the Runway Gen-4 negative-phrasing sentence and the Imagen subject/context/style guidance through repeated web-search excerpts of the vendor pages (those hosts were unreachable directly), confirmed the AmbiEnt figures and the Mars Climate Orbiter findings (NASA's November 10, 1999 release of the board's findings) by search, relied on expert knowledge for ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018, Sclar et al. (ICLR 2024), Min et al. (EMNLP 2022), WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3 and the Cucumber Book, checked figure numbering against the app's renderer (figures are numbered in section order), tested each of the 11 Prompt kit templates against the chapter's own advice, and re-solved all 16 multiple-choice keys, both sort exercises (20 items) and the order exercise blind before comparing.

corrections.quote: Most vague words in prompts can be translated (Figure 1.4).
corrections.correction: Most vague words in prompts can be translated (Figure 1.3).
corrections.why: The app numbers figures in section order (dr-professor.html figHTML increments figNo per section). The section 1.3 figure (ch1-fig-4.svg, feeling-to-check) renders as Figure 1.3, so the text points to the wrong figure.

corrections.quote: build, check every acceptance criterion, revise (Figure 1.3).
corrections.correction: build, check every acceptance criterion, revise (Figure 1.4).
corrections.why: The section 1.4 figure (ch1-fig-3.svg, the build-check-revise loop) is the fourth figure in section order and renders as Figure 1.4.

corrections.quote: Anthropic’s guide notes that recent Claude models respond more strongly to instructions than earlier ones
corrections.correction: Anthropic’s guide notes that some recent Claude models (it names Claude Opus 4.5 and 4.6) are more responsive to the system prompt than earlier ones
corrections.why: The live page (checked October 12, 2026) says: “Claude Opus 4.5 and Claude Opus 4.6 are also more responsive to the system prompt than previous models... may now overtrigger.” It names those two models and the system prompt, not recent models and instructions in general. The quoted CRITICAL/MUST wording is verbatim.

corrections.quote: Do not start the task yet. Read my request below the way a capable stranger would.
corrections.correction: Before you start the task, read my request below the way a capable stranger would.
corrections.why: The chapter's own advice (1.1 reading, Anthropic: tell the model what to do instead of what not to do) asks for positive phrasing; the template opens with a prohibition. The rewrite keeps the meaning.

corrections.quote: Space: dry and close, with no echo or room sound.
corrections.correction: Space: dry and close, as if recorded right next to the source.
corrections.why: This line is pasted into a sound generator, the kind of model the chapter warns handles negation badly (1.1 reading on Runway; the template kit's own Negatives to positives tool). Naming “echo” and “room sound” can pull them in. The positive description says the same thing.

corrections.quote: Under 1 second, dry, one sound only; no music or voice.
corrections.correction: Under 1 second, dry, a single isolated sound effect on its own.
corrections.why: The model answer is a prompt for a sound-effect generator but uses a prohibition (“no music or voice”), which contradicts the chapter's positive-phrasing advice for generative media models.

corrections.quote: Output format: “WAV, mono, 48 kHz, three variations.”
corrections.correction: Output format: “WAV, mono, 48 kHz, three variations” (a delivery choice for this project, set in the generator’s export settings or by converting afterwards, since prompt text rarely controls the file format).
corrections.why: WAV, mono and 48 kHz are reasonable project choices, not universal requirements. Most sound generators set format, sample rate and variation count through controls or plans rather than prompt text (the chapter's own Sound-effect brief note says so). Without that framing the answer suggests typing the format into the prompt will produce it.

corrections.quote: Where does it run? In which language?
corrections.correction: Where does it run, and in which language? Who lays out the platforms?
corrections.why: Step 3 promises to decide or delegate “each one” but then delegates the platform layout, which is not on the list. Figure 1.1 shows eight decisions that include Platform layout and not language. The merged question keeps the count at eight (step 2) and makes the list match both step 3 and Figure 1.1.

corrections.quote: the output format is a PNG at 1920×1080 in four variations
corrections.correction: the output format is four variations as 16:9 PNGs, resized or upscaled to 1920×1080 if the tool’s native size is smaller
corrections.why: Few image generators output exactly 1920×1080. Their native 16:9 sizes are usually smaller or different, for example Imagen's 1408×768 and Midjourney's 1456×816 at default settings. As written, the spec asks the tool for a size it usually cannot produce directly. The template note already says size is set through the tool's controls.

The row is for soft painted title art. A generated painted image always contains blends and anti-aliased edges, so a check that only four colors appear fails for every result. A tolerant check that the dominant colors match the palette is one that can actually pass or fail.

summary: Every Anthropic quotation (the brilliant-new-employee framing, golden rule, can-you-suggest example, ellipses example, CRITICAL/MUST, examples wording, prefill 400 on Claude 4.6+, Claude Code verification, interview and clean-session lines) matches the live pages. The OpenAI GPT-5.5, Runway Gen-4 and Imagen claims match vendor-page excerpts, and all 37 keys agree. The fixes are two swapped figure cross-references (1.3 and 1.4), one over-generalized Anthropic attribution, and seven alignment fixes so the templates, model answers, worked-example list and image checks follow the chapter's own positive-phrasing and tool-control advice.
